pronunciation: m (a nasal hum, like saying 'hmm') + tea
meaning: "I don't know"; "dunno" — used alone as a reply, or to preface an uncertain guess

example.english: I don't know where he went.

note: Said by itself, 毋知 is a very common one-word answer (like English "dunno"), and it also shows up sentence-initially as a hedge, e.g. 毋知會毋會落雨 ("I wonder if it'll rain").
